title: Instagram's crackdown on AI glasses creeps is off to a bumpy start
excerpt: Instagram said it would remove harassing videos filmed with Meta AI glasses. Weeks later, dozens remain.
content_html:
"Are you a secret code?" a young man in Meta glasses asks a woman in a tank top on the sidewalk. "What do you mean, 'a secret code?'" she responds, seemingly confused as the man's glasses record her. "Because I'm trying to crack you," he says.

The interaction, filmed by content creator Colin Allen for his Instagram account @thatiscolin, is one of dozens of similar videos that I found from popular and verified accounts on the platform in the month after Instagram boss Adam Mosseri said Meta would remove "harassing" pickup line videos filmed with Meta glasses.

After I sent Meta a link to 20-plus pickup and other harassing "prank" videos from different accounts, the company removed the "secret code" video and eight others. Allen, who describes himself as a "lifestyle and comedy creator" and not a pickup artist, had used the same line to different women in several other videos, which remain up.

Videos from pickup artists using Meta glasses to approach women in public have emerged as a genre on Instagram's Reels and TikTok, with some of the popular videos racking up millions of views. These videos of men trying pickup lines on women on the street, along with pranks on cashiers or service workers, are tagged on Instagram as being shot on "Meta glasses."

Being associated with that kind of icky content can't be good for the reputation of the devices, which some people are already referring to as "creep glasses."

Tracy Clayton, a spokesperson for Meta, told me that thousands of pieces of content have already been removed, and several large accounts have been taken down. The recent enforcement action falls under Meta's existing Community Standards on bullying and harassment, which broadly forbid content that sexualizes other adults or sexually harasses people. Additionally, search terms for "rizz" or "cold approach," common pickup slang, are now blocked in search.

My last month spent in pickup-line video land has shown me that Meta's enforcement has been uneven in the weeks since Mosseri's remarks. "We don't want people to be surreptitiously taking videos of other people and harassing them and then posting them on our platform. So we're trying to fight that every way we can," Mosseri said in mid-July.

When initially reporting on Mosseri's comments, I found two large pickup artist accounts that had been deactivated as part of the recent enforcement wave. A few days after my article was published last month, one of those accounts was reactivated (a Meta spokesperson said this was by error, and the account was re-banned after I brought it to their attention).

Carolina Are, a digital criminologist based at the London School of Economics and Political Science, said that Meta and Mosseri's response to the harassing AI glasses videos highlights isn't enough.

"There is a backlash, and then Meta tends to minimize its own responsibility for it. They talk about how this is user-generated behavior or an error in enforcement," Are said. "But they don't recognize the systemic issues that are causing that to happen, and they take no accountability for what their policies or infrastructure have done to enable that behavior," Are said.

These pickup and prank videos made with Meta glasses aren't exclusive to Instagram; they also exist on YouTube and TikTok.

A spokesperson for TikTok told me that it has policies against harassing content. After I sent a list of four videos of pickup artists who also posted on Instagram, TikTok took down two of them, citing its policy on bullying and sexual harassment.

Boot Bullwinkle, a representative for YouTube, told me it has policies against certain kinds of harassment and dangerous prank videos. YouTube has been dealing with moderation issues around street pranks and pickup artists for years. After I sent four examples of channels that posted Meta glasses pickup content, YouTube said it took down "several" of the videos and removed one of the channels from its monetization program.

A headache of its own making

Mosseri personally delivering the message that Instagram will take down this specific kind of content is unique among video platforms. That may be because of Instagram's unique relationship with the Meta glasses: Not only are these unsavory videos a headache of its own making, but they also risk harming the public perception of a product that Meta invested big bucks in building and marketing.

Plenty of people are buying up Meta's AI glasses. Sales have grown since their launch in 2021, topping 7 million units in 2025, more than triple the previous year. Meta is the early leader in the smart glasses race.

They've been a bright spot for Meta's money-losing Reality Labs department, which faced layoffs this year. They're also key to CEO Mark Zuckerberg's AI bet.

"I think in the future, if you don't have glasses that have AI or some way to interact with AI, I think you're kind of similarly, probably [going to] be at a pretty significant cognitive disadvantage compared to other people and who you're working with, or competing against," Zuckerberg said in a 2025 earnings call.

The recent backlash — remember when Kylie Jenner's Instagram comments were flooded with people calling her signature Meta glasses "pervert glasses"? — presents a thorn in Meta's side.

"In many cases, the public-facing rules that users see are vague enough to be open to the discretion of the platform to make those kinds of shifts and changes at any time," said Sarah T. Roberts, faculty director and cofounder of the UCLA Center for Critical Internet Inquiry.

Meta is betting AI could supercharge its moderation efforts. Zuckerberg and other execs have long said the old way of doing things, leaning heavily on third-party human contractors, doesn't scale. The theory goes that AI can be trained to autonomously flag violating content. In June, Meta told the Financial Times that initial tests showed that its AI systems made fewer mistakes than human moderators and flagged more violating content. The jury's still out on whether that will prove to be the case long term.

Deactivated one day, reactivated the next

After seeking out and interacting with some of these pickup line videos in Reels, I started getting served more and more of them. I no longer needed search terms to find them; my Reels feed was filled nearly entirely with that genre of content.

One creator whose account was active weeks after Mosseri's remarks is Caren Babaknia. He has 174,000 followers and posts videos of himself driving up to women he identifies in the caption as escorts and talking to them while wearing Meta glasses.

In one video captioned "Wasting ESCORTS time by making them watch brainrot" he offers a woman who approached his car $50 in exchange for watching a video on his laptop of brainrot memes. The woman agrees, and he plays the video, which includes an ad for a gambling app. He hands her the cash.

I spoke with Babaknia on the phone to get his perspective on videos made with Meta glasses. He told me he believes the women in his videos are aware that he was filming them because his content is so viral that they knew him.

He voiced disdain for pickup artists with Meta glasses, however.

"I think the rizz content is very cringe," he told me. "I think those are normal girls and they don't deserve to be videoed without their consent."

After including one of Babaknia's videos in the list I recently sent to Meta, his account was deactivated the following morning. Babaknia told me that he was going to appeal. A day later, his account was back up with the videos restored.

It's not unusual for changes to enforcement in content moderation to take time to implement at scale. But as Meta glasses get increasingly popular, it seems likely that Instagram will face pressure to deal with this — and potentially new forms of bad behavior — more and more.

"It's not like they just started those platforms yesterday," said Roberts from UCLA. "It's not like they don't have 20 years now of understanding how people will behave at the most depraved levels if given a chance."

sentences.en: Instagram

content_html_zh:
“你是暗号吗？” 一位戴着 Meta 眼镜的年轻男子向人行道上一位穿着背心的女士询问。 “‘密码’是什么意思？”她回答道，当男人的眼镜记录下她的情况时，她似乎很困惑。 “因为我想破解你，”他说。

这段互动由内容创作者 Colin Allen 为他的 Instagram 账户 @thatiscolin 拍摄，是 Instagram 老板 Adam Mosseri 表示 Meta 将删除用 Meta 眼镜拍摄的“骚扰”搭讪视频的一个月后，我从该平台上受欢迎且经过验证的账户中发现的数十个类似视频之一。

在我向 Meta 发送了来自不同帐户的 20 多个搭便车和其他骚扰性“恶作剧”视频的链接后，该公司删除了“密码”视频和其他 8 个视频。 艾伦将自己描述为“生活方式和喜剧创造者”，而不是把妹达人，他在其他几个视频中对不同的女性使用了同样的台词，这些视频仍然保留着。

搭讪艺术家使用 Meta 眼镜在公共场合接近女性的视频已成为 Instagram 的 Reels 和 TikTok 上的一种类型，其中一些热门视频的观看次数达到了数百万次。 这些男性试图在街上搭讪女性的视频，以及对收银员或服务人员的恶作剧，在 Instagram 上被标记为使用“Meta 眼镜”拍摄。

与这种令人讨厌的内容联系在一起对这些设备的声誉不利，有些人已经将其称为“令人毛骨悚然的眼镜”。

Meta 发言人特雷西·克莱顿 (Tracy Clayton) 告诉我，数千条内容已被删除，多个大型账户也已被删除。 最近的执法行动属于 Meta 现有的关于欺凌和骚扰的社区标准，该标准广泛禁止使其他成年人性化或性骚扰他人的内容。 此外，“rizz”或“冷方法”（常见的拾音俚语）的搜索词现在在搜索中被屏蔽。

上个月在拾音视频领域的经历让我看到，自 Mosseri 发表言论以来的几周内，Meta 的执法力度一直不平衡。 “我们不希望人们偷偷拍摄其他人的视频并骚扰他们，然后将其发布到我们的平台上。 因此，我们正在尽一切努力来应对这一问题，”莫塞里在 7 月中旬说道。

当最初报道莫塞里的评论时，我发现两个大型把妹达人账户在最近的执法浪潮中已被停用。 上个月我的文章发表几天后，其中一个帐户被重新激活（一位 Meta 发言人表示这是一个错误，在我提请他们注意后，该帐户被重新禁止）。

伦敦政治经济学院的数字犯罪学家 Carolina Are 表示，Meta 和 Mosseri 对骚扰性 AI 眼镜视频集锦的回应还不够。

“存在强烈反对，然后 Meta 往往会尽量减少自己的责任。 他们谈论这是用户生成的行为或执行错误，”阿雷说。 “但他们没有认识到导致这种情况发生的系统性问题，而且他们对他们的政策或基础设施为实现这种行为所做的事情不承担任何责任，”阿雷说。

这些用 Meta 眼镜制作的搭讪和恶作剧视频并不是 Instagram 独有的。它们也存在于 YouTube 和 TikTok 上。

TikTok 的一位发言人告诉我，它有针对骚扰内容的政策。 在我发送了也在 Instagram 上发布的四个把妹达人的视频列表后，TikTok 删除了其中两个视频，理由是其关于欺凌和性骚扰的政策。

YouTube 的代表 Boot Bullwinkle 告诉我，该公司制定了针对某些类型的骚扰和危险恶作剧视频的政策。 多年来，YouTube 一直在处理有关街头恶作剧和把妹艺术家的审核问题。 在我发送了四个发布 Meta 眼镜拾取内容的频道示例后，YouTube 表示它删除了“几个”视频，并从其盈利计划中删除了其中一个频道。

自己造成的头痛

Mosseri 亲自传达 Instagram 将删除此类特定内容的信息，这在视频平台中是独一无二的。 这可能是因为 Instagram 与 Meta 眼镜的独特关系：这些令人讨厌的视频不仅是其自己制作的令人头疼的问题，而且还可能损害公众对 Meta 投入巨资打造和营销的产品的看法。

很多人都在购买 Meta 的人工智能眼镜。 自 2021 年推出以来，销量不断增长，到 2025 年销量将突破 700 万台，是上一年的三倍多。 Meta 是智能眼镜竞赛的早期领导者。

它们一直是 Meta 亏损的现实实验室部门的亮点，该部门今年面临裁员。 它们也是首席执行官马克扎克伯格的人工智能赌注的关键。

扎克伯格在 2025 年财报电话会议上表示：“我认为，在未来，如果你没有带有人工智能或某种方式与人工智能交互的眼镜，我认为与其他人以及与你一起工作或竞争的人相比，你可能会处于相当显着的认知劣势。”

最近的强烈反对——还记得凯莉·詹纳 (Kylie Jenner) 的 Instagram 评论充斥着人们称她标志性的 Meta 眼镜为“变态眼镜”吗？ — 是 Meta 的眼中钉。

“在许多情况下，用户看到的面向公众的规则足够模糊，平台可以自行决定随时做出此类转变和改变，”Sarah T. 罗伯茨是加州大学洛杉矶分校关键互联网探究中心的教务主任兼联合创始人。

Meta 押注人工智能可以增强其审核工作。 扎克伯格和其他高管长期以来一直表示，严重依赖第三方承包商的旧做事方式无法扩大规模。 该理论认为，人工智能可以被训练来自动标记违规内容。 今年 6 月，Meta 告诉英国《金融时报》，初步测试表明，其人工智能系统比人类审核员犯的错误更少，并标记了更多违规内容。 从长远来看，这种情况是否会持续下去，目前还没有定论。

某天停用，第二天又恢复

在 Reels 中寻找并与其中一些搭讪视频进行互动后，我开始获得越来越多的服务。 我不再需要搜索词来找到它们；我的 Reels feed 几乎完全充满了这种类型的内容。

在莫塞里发表言论几周后，卡伦·巴巴克尼亚 (Caren Babaknia) 的账户就活跃起来了。 他拥有 174,000 名粉丝，并发布了自己驾车走向他在标题中标识为护送的女性的视频，并戴着 Meta 眼镜与她们交谈。

在一段题为“让护送人员观看脑腐病片浪费时间”的视频中，他向一名走近他汽车的女士提供 50 美元，以换取他在笔记本电脑上观看脑腐病模因的视频。 该女子同意了，他播放了视频，其中包括赌博应用程序的广告。 他把现金递给她。

我通过电话与 Babaknia 进行了交谈，了解他对使用 Meta 眼镜制作的视频的看法。 他告诉我，他相信他视频中的女性知道他在拍摄她们，因为他的内容如此火爆，以至于她们都认识他。

不过，他对戴着 Meta 眼镜的把妹达人表示不屑。

“我认为 rizz 的内容非常令人畏惧，”他告诉我。 “我认为这些都是正常的女孩，未经她们同意，不应该被录像。”

在我最近发送给 Meta 的列表中添加了 Babaknia 的一个视频后，他的帐户第二天早上就被停用了。 巴巴克尼亚告诉我他要上诉。 一天后，他的帐户恢复了，视频也恢复了。

内容审核执行方面的改变需要时间才能大规模实施，这并不罕见。 但随着 Meta 眼镜越来越受欢迎，Instagram 似乎将面临越来越大的压力来应对这一问题——以及潜在的新形式的不良行为。

“他们不像昨天才启动这些平台，”加州大学洛杉矶分校的罗伯茨说。 “他们并不是没有 20 年的时间来了解，如果有机会的话，人们会在最堕落的层面上做出怎样的行为。”
